value: lowest behavioural threshold about 0.6 mV/cm (peak-to-peak), found close to but not exactly at the electric-organ discharge fundamental frequency
method: food-rewarded conditioning: fish swam to a sine-wave field whose frequency was clamped to its own electric-organ discharge, thresholds interpolated at 70 % of trials responded to
conditions: Eigenmannia sp. from a commercial dealer, 9 fish 11-20 cm long, kept at 27 C; water conductivity 100 (unit garbled in the PDF text layer); 0.6 mV/cm was the lowest value in the study, from fish no. 1 at 0.99 and 1.01 times the discharge frequency; the authors call thresholds relative (modulation thresholds), not absolute

source.title: Electrosensory Stimulus-Intensity Thresholds in the Weakly Electric Knifefish Eigenmannia: Reduced Sensitivity at Harmonics of its own Organ Discharge

quote: Over the wide frequency range investigated [...], the lowest stimulus-intensity thresholds of 0.6 mV cm-1 (peak-to-peak) (0 dB) at a water conductivity of 100 mS cm-1 were found close to (but not exactly at) the EOD fundamental frequency.
note: The species is given only as Eigenmannia sp., so the record is at genus rank and grade g. Quote normalised from the PDF text layer, which printed cm-1 as 'cm21' and garbled the conductivity unit; the bracketed ellipsis stands for '(0.3–3.01 times EOD frequency)'. The Discussion puts the lowest values (0.6, 0.9 and 1.1 mV/cm) in the same range as a 1992 report of 0.3-0.6 mV/cm and says the authors used a lower, more natural conductivity than that earlier work. The minimum comes from a single fish; means are higher (see the DF record).

value: threshold 1.27 mV/cm at a stimulus 1 Hz above the fish's own discharge frequency, 25.07 mV/cm when the stimulus matched it exactly (about 20 dB higher)
method: food-rewarded conditioning with a stimulus clamped to a set frequency difference (DF) from the electric-organ discharge
conditions: Eigenmannia sp., this experiment N=6 fish 11 cm long (one-way ANOVA d.f.=17); water about 100 conductivity units as in the paper; threshold depended significantly on DF (F=15.154, P<0.0003); unclamped jamming-avoidance tests gave larger threshold rises (up to 32 dB) than the clamped ones (up to 15 dB)

source.title: Electrosensory Stimulus-Intensity Thresholds in the Weakly Electric Knifefish Eigenmannia: Reduced Sensitivity at Harmonics of its own Organ Discharge

quote: Mean threshold intensities (± S.E.M.) were 25.07±11.33 mVp–p cm-1 for DF=0 Hz, 2.46±1.03 mVp–p cm-1 for DF=-1 Hz and 1.27±0.17 mVp–p cm-1 for DF=+1 Hz; threshold intensity depended significantly on DF (F=15.154; P<0.0003; d.f.=17; one-way ANOVA).
note: Species given only as Eigenmannia sp. (genus rank, grade g). Quote normalised from the PDF text layer, which printed cm-1 as 'cm21' and the minus sign of DF=-1 as '21'. The mean at DF=0 carries a large standard error (11.33). The authors read the rise at exact frequency identity as insensitivity at integer harmonics of the discharge, which the jamming avoidance response helps the fish avoid.

value: most sensitive neural response at 80 kHz, threshold 54.9 dB SPL (mean, s.e. 1.0)
eye: tympanal ear; A1 receptor cell in the auditory nerve
method: extracellular recording from the tympanal nerve with ultrasonic pulses (criterion: two or more spikes in at least 8 of 10 stimuli); laser Doppler vibrometry of the tympanal membrane from 50 to 300 kHz at 90 dB SPL
conditions: laboratory greater wax moths, 20 moths for the nerve thresholds (10 of each sex); only the A1 cell was analysed; laser vibrometry peaks were about 90-95 kHz in females and 125 kHz in males, a sex difference the authors found not significant

source.authors: Moir HM, Jackson JC, Windmill JFC
source.title: Extremely high frequency sensitivity in a 'simple' ear

quote: The greatest neural sensitivity of our measurements was at 80 kHz (54.9±1.0 dB SPL; mean±s.e., n = 20), matching earlier studies [9].
note: Quote normalised from the PDF text layer (plus-minus and equals signs). The vibrometry peak and the neural best frequency differ, and the paper does not reconcile them in the sentences read.

value: auditory nerve responded to pulses at 280 kHz (threshold 82.9 dB SPL, n=18) and at 300 kHz (86.8 dB SPL, n=15); 5 of 20 moths gave no spikes at 300 kHz and 90 dB SPL
eye: tympanal ear; A1 receptor cell in the auditory nerve
method: extracellular recording from the tympanal nerve; highest test frequency 300 kHz, loudest level 90 dB SPL
conditions: 20 moths tested; the threshold means are for the moths that responded; higher sound levels were not tested, so non-responders might respond at higher levels; no behavioural test was made
